name: Bai lan (摆烂)
blurb: Chinese slang for "letting it rot": giving up on something that won't get better
title: Bai Lan (摆烂) Meaning: Chinese Slang for Letting It Rot
description: Bai lan (摆烂), "let it rot", means giving up on a situation that won't improve. It comes from the Chinese term for NBA tanking.
h1: What does bai lan (摆烂) mean?
answer: Bai lan (摆烂, bǎi làn) means deciding a situation is beyond saving and no longer trying, just letting it get worse; it is often translated "let it rot". The term comes from basketball: some NBA teams deliberately lose to finish last and get a better draft pick, which American sports call tanking and Chinese sports media translated as 摆烂. It moved into everyday slang and was everywhere around 2022.

body: In the NBA, a team that knows it can't contend may lose on purpose to finish near the bottom and improve its draft position. In English that is tanking; Chinese sports coverage rendered it as 摆烂.

From sports and esports the word spread into daily life, broadening into "things are going badly, so I'll just give up". When 咬文嚼字 picked its 2022 buzzwords, editor-in-chief Huang Anjing said 摆烂 ranked near the top in their word-frequency survey but was left off the list because of its negative meaning.

ul: 这周作业太多了，我直接摆烂 (too much homework this week; I'm just letting it rot)
减肥第三天，看到火锅后选择摆烂 (day three of my diet, saw hot pot, gave up)
比分落后二十分，这队已经开始摆烂了 (down twenty points, the team has stopped trying)
摆烂一时爽，一直摆烂一直爽 (giving up feels good once, and good every time)
今天也是摆烂的一天 (another day of letting it rot)

body: Most people saying 我摆烂了 ("I've given up") are joking or venting, not actually abandoning everything. Among friends that is normal.
Saying someone else 在摆烂 ("is letting it rot") is a real criticism: it says they are being irresponsible. Use it carefully about colleagues or teams.

faq.q: What is bai lan in English?
faq.a: In sports it is tanking. In everyday use it is usually translated "let it rot", or "give up and let things slide".
Yes, mostly. About yourself it is self-mockery; about someone else it is criticism.

faq.q: Was 摆烂 a buzzword of the year?
faq.a: It was very frequent in 2022, but 咬文嚼字 left it off its top 10 list because of its negative meaning.
